original_question: Characterize those ordered Banach spaces X whose cone X+ is non-normal but for which every increasing weakly convergent sequence is nevertheless norm convergent.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Open Problem 6.5: Characterize those ordered Banach spaces (with non-normal cone) in which every increasing weakly convergent sequence is norm convergent.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It correctly focuses on ordered Banach spaces, assumes the cone is non-normal, asks for a characterization, and stays with increasing weakly convergent sequences rather than drifting to a broader neighboring problem.
missing_details: State the paper's ambient setting: X is a real ordered Banach space.
Specify that the order is induced by a closed cone X_+.
Define 'increasing sequence' as x_n <= x_{n+1} for all n with respect to that order.
Make explicit that weak convergence and norm convergence are both taken in X.
If you want the question to be fully stand-alone, spell out non-normality: there is no constant C >= 0 such that 0 <= x <= y implies ||x|| <= C||y|| for all x,y in X.
Do not broaden the question from sequences to nets; the paper treats the net version separately as Open Problem 6.2.
To remain paper-faithful, keep in view the nearby partial obstruction from Theorem 6.3: the property fails whenever X_+ is non-normal and X''_+ is a cone, in particular when X is reflexive.
refined_question: Let X be a real ordered Banach space ordered by a closed cone X_+, and assume that X_+ is non-normal, i.e. there is no constant C >= 0 such that 0 <= x <= y implies ||x|| <= C||y|| for all x,y in X. Characterize those such spaces for which every increasing sequence (x_n) in X, meaning x_n <= x_{n+1} for all n, that converges weakly in X is automatically norm convergent.
justification: This is exactly the paper's Open Problem 6.5 in Section 6. The surrounding discussion matters: Example 6.1 shows the phenomenon is non-vacuous by using a Schur space with a non-normal cone; Open Problem 6.2 treats the different net version; and Theorem 6.3 gives a partial negative criterion by ruling out all non-normal spaces whose bidual wedge X''_+ is a cone, in particular all reflexive ones. Proposition 5.2 is the characterization of the condition that X''_+ be a cone used in the proof of Theorem 6.3. So the refined question should stay narrowly in the sequence setting and include the paper's conventions on order and normality.
